bullets: **Fan** (Stave 2): rescues young Scrooge, ‘home, for good and all’: loving family.
**Belle’s family** (Stave 2): a noisy, happy home with children; Scrooge realises he could have had this.
**The Cratchits** (Stave 3): close, loving, mutually supportive in poverty.
**Fred**: Scrooge’s only family, rejected until Stave 5.
Scrooge’s **isolation**: no family, no friends; ‘solitary as an oyster’.
Fezziwig’s ball includes everyone, from the housemaid to the baker: social harmony across classes.
Stave 3 streets: shops overflowing, people greeting each other, a sense of shared joy.
Miners, lighthouse keepers, sailors: Christmas unites people even in isolated places.
Stave 4: the dead man (Scrooge) is mourned by no one: the cost of rejecting community.
Stave 5: Scrooge walks the streets, greets people, goes to church: reintegration.
The Ghost of Christmas Present embodies it.
Tiny Tim’s ‘God bless us every one’ expresses it.
Scrooge’s vow: ‘I will honour Christmas in my heart, and try to keep it all the year.’

callouts.p: Dickens presents family and community as the true sources of happiness, and Christmas as the season that reminds people of their bonds to each other, especially to the poor.

core.p: For Dickens, Christmas means generosity, forgiveness, warmth, family and care for the poor.

model: Context: Victorian family ideal, Dickens’s childhood
exam.q: Explain the importance of family elsewhere in the novella. (20 marks)
exam.tip: Frame as Scrooge’s journey from isolation to belonging.

mistakes.r: It is a moral standard against which characters are judged.

quotes.q: There never was such a goose

quotes.a: Christmas values as a way of life.

summary: Family, community and the Christmas spirit are shown through Fan, Fezziwig, the Cratchits, Fred’s party and the scenes of shared celebration in Stave 3; Scrooge’s isolation contrasts with these, and his redemption is completed when he rejoins family and community.
